I am currently exploring opportunities where I can apply and learn more about causal inference. I hold a [Master of Science in Statistics](https://www.ku.dk/studies/masters/statistics) from the [University of Copenhagen](https://www.ku.dk/en). A big part of my master's, more than half, was spent studying causal discovery and causal inference. Before that, I obtained a [Bachelor of Science in Mathematics](https://www.mathematics.uni-bonn.de/studium/en/study-programs/bachelor-mathematik) from the [University of Bonn](https://www.uni-bonn.de/en/home) with a focus on numerical mathematics and statistics. Outside of academia, I enjoy demanding sports, as they provide a good balance to theoretical work and help me stay motivated and maintain a strong work ethic. I competed in fencing for over ten years and attended a [sports high school](https://sportgymnasium-jena.info/). I also enjoy reading classic literature, baking, and cooking with friends. On this website, I share what I am currently working on, what I have been working on in the past, and what I am interested in. ## Research interests {#research_interests}
Causal inference Assumptions and study design Semiparametric theory Nonparametric statistics TMLE DML Heterogeneous treatment effects Tree-based methods Ensemble methods Online experimentation
Broadly, I am interested in causal inference and issues that arise when applying causal inference methods. More specifically, I am interested in assumption violations and how different study designs rely on different sets of assumptions to obtain valid causal estimates. In the context of estimation, I find semiparametric theory compelling. I more drawn to targeted maximum likelihood estimation (TMLE), while also being interested in double/debiased machine learning (DML). Besides biostatistics and economics, two prominent fields of application for causal inference, I am also looking to explore online experimentation, including A/B testing. As causal inference is a relatively young field, it offers many opportunities for methodological advances and for integrating causal methods into a wide range of other fields. In the longer term, I hope to pursue research that involves these developments and their applications. Overall, I see causal inference as a means of better understanding and modelling the world and thereby answering important questions. ## News {#news} - **October 2026:**    My personal website is online.
